newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian Hansapank started option trade.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Hansapank started option trade.

text.p: Largest Baltic bank, Estonia's Hansapank, has started OTC option trading which has sparked strong interest from local buyers, the bank said on Wednesday.
Trading began in January and includes share as well as currency options.
Hansapank is one of the first banks in the Baltics to start derivatives trading, especially in shares as stock markets are relatively new in the region.
"Local investors were very interested and looked for good returns, especially when the market was volatile in the first week of options trade," Hansapank analyst Katrin Kaarli said.
The first options buyers received good returns but the market has now settled down and returns are not so good, she added. Hansapank is the only Estonian bank trading in options.
Estonia opened a stock market in May 1996 and the bourse now trades 15 stocks split into an official and OTC list.
Buyers of equity options are only locals at present. Hansapank trades both European and American options.
European options can only be exercised on the expiry date while American options can be exercised at any time, up to and including expiry.
Hansapank also trades FX options on Estonian kroon/German mark and kroon/Finnish markka for foreign investors.
